name: gtk-settings
description: The GtkSettings keys the settings application's Fonts & Icons and Appearance pages write into ~/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini and ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini, with the value domain GTK itself accepts for each one. A key that is not listed here is not written, and tests/test_settings_gtk_keys.py fails if the application names one.
_note: This record exists because the Fonts & Icons page has to change something that survives a logout, and the compositor's config leaves do not reach GTK applications: a font family set with hyprctl eval would be a value nothing reads. GtkSettings is the mechanism GTK reads at startup on a session with no GNOME settings daemon, the file is plain INI under the user's own config directory, and the frozen v4 payload already used it (legacy/config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini), so this is not a new idea in this project -- it is the same one, with each key now verified against the release this project pins instead of inherited.

gtk4.what: gtk/gtksettings.c: every property name below appears as a g_param_spec_* call at the line cited, and the value domain is the one that call declares

gtk3.what: the same property names are GtkSettings properties in GTK 3, which is why the two settings.ini files can carry the same keys; this project's own frozen v4 payload already writes six of them (legacy/config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini)
gtk3.unverified_note: TODO(verify) SET-05 in docs/UNVERIFIED.md: the GTK 3 property table was not read out of a pinned 3.24 ref this pass. The six keys the legacy payload writes are evidence they exist, and the application writes GTK 3 keys only from that same set.

file_format.what: settings.ini is an INI file with one [Settings] section; GtkSettings reads it through GKeyFile, so a key is written as name=value with no quoting and no comment support inside a value
file_format.evidence: GNOME/gtk@4.10.0:gtk/gtksettings.c gtk_settings_load_files() and the legacy payload legacy/config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini

source: GNOME/gtk at 4.10.0: gtk/gtksettings.c -- every g_param_spec_* declaration below, and the strcmp chains at :1442-1448 and :1458-1466 that decide which spellings of the hint style and subpixel order are accepted; this repository's own frozen v4 payload legacy/config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini for the GTK 3 keys it already writes

files.note: Not a generated file: it carries no GENERATED header and is not rendered from tokens, because it holds the user's own choices rather than a preset's. The Part 2 sheets in the same directory are generated and say so.
Written with the same keys, limited to the set the frozen v4 payload already used, because GTK 3 applications still read this file and a font change that only reached GTK 4 would look like a bug.

gtk-font-name.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's UI font row

gtk-xft-antialias.value_note: -1 is the system default, 0 is off, 1 is on. Declared by g_param_spec_int with exactly that range.
gtk-xft-antialias.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's antialiasing row

gtk-xft-hinting.value_note: -1 is the system default, 0 is off, 1 is on.
gtk-xft-hinting.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's hinting switch

gtk-xft-hintstyle.value_note: Compared with strcmp against exactly these four spellings; anything else leaves the hint style at Cairo's default rather than raising, which is why the application offers a dropdown and never a text entry.
gtk-xft-hintstyle.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's hinting strength row

gtk-xft-rgba.value_note: Subpixel order. A value outside the four leaves CAIRO_SUBPIXEL_ORDER_DEFAULT in place, so an unrecognised spelling is silently ignored -- recorded here so the application lists four options and no free text.
gtk-xft-rgba.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's subpixel order row

gtk-icon-theme-name.default: the DEFAULT_ICON_THEME constant, which is Adwaita
gtk-icon-theme-name.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's icon theme row

gtk-cursor-theme-name.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's cursor theme row

gtk-cursor-theme-size.value_note: 0 means the system default, which is why the row's lowest position is 0 and not 16.
gtk-cursor-theme-size.used_by: the Fonts & Icons page's cursor size row

gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme.used_by: the Appearance page's dark mode switch, which also drives libadwaita's own colour scheme so the two cannot disagree

gtk-theme-name.note: Recorded and deliberately not written. The GTK theme this session uses is applied by iarch-theme through the generated sheets and the installer's package choice, so a second writer of gtk-theme-name would be a second source of truth for the same decision.

gtk-enable-animations.note: Recorded and deliberately not written. Reduce motion in this project is the animation.reduce_motion switch, which iarch-anim owns and which renders every transition at 0ms in the Part 2 sheets; setting this key as well would give one intention two mechanisms that can disagree.

rejected.why: The GNOME schema is not guaranteed to exist on a Hyprland session, and gsettings is not installed in this repository's CI, so a change made that way could not be verified or rolled back. settings.ini is a file this project can read, back up and restore with the machinery it already has.
rejected.evidence: no gsettings binary in the development environment; GtkSettings reads settings.ini directly (GNOME/gtk@4.10.0:gtk/gtksettings.c)

rejected.spelling: a hyprctl eval that sets a font or an icon theme
rejected.why: The compositor's config leaves are about compositing: there is no font-family leaf, and an eval cannot reach a GTK application's settings. Writing one would be a value nothing reads.
rejected.evidence: data/design/tokens.json hyprland.leaves lists all 41 leaves this project may set, and none of them is a font or an icon theme
